digest.component_or_area: LLM provider configuration and model resolution
propositions: Provider qualification is currently decided by regex shape matching (`^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$`) rather than membership in a known registry, causing typo'd configured providers to be accepted at config time and later fail at construction.

The shape test silently promotes any colon-prefixed model string with a dotless-identifier prefix to a qualified provider, breaking canonical Bedrock IDs like `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` and masking future model ID shape changes.
Replace the shape regex with a static `KNOWN_PROVIDER_NAMES` frozenset of 24 registry members, deciding qualification by membership not shape, matching pydantic-ai's runtime semantics.

Configured providers must be validated against the registry and raise `LLMConfigError` at config-resolution time; inline prefixes that are not members fall back to unqualified (permissive, preserves colon-bearing model IDs intact).

Two de-registered names (`test` and `google_genai`) are neither in pydantic-ai nor any rebar builder registry and must not be grandfathered; slashed names (`gateway/openai`, etc.) that the old regex rejected are now correctly accepted.
